cards.text: Welcome back, baker! Psalm 119 keeps going, and the psalm's writer is still talking straight to the LORD about His word. This time he starts LOW. He says his soul cleaves to the dust, and friend, I know that floor. I lived under a takeout menu for years.

cards.question: Down in the dust, the writer asks the LORD to revive him according to His word.

cards.text: Then he says he laid out his ways before God, and God ANSWERED him. I can't get my group chat to answer, and this man is getting answers from heaven.

cards.question: After God answers him, what does the writer ask for?

answers.text: To be shown a sign from heaven
To be given a long and full life

cards.text: Next he asks God to make the way of His precepts clear to him. Like a recipe card when somebody finally wipes the dough smudge off the oven temperature.

cards.question: Once God's precepts are clear to him, what does the writer say he will do?

cards.text: Then it gets heavier. He says his soul melts with sorrow, and baker, that is cookie-left-on-the-dashboard-in-July melted.

cards.question: Melting with sorrow, the writer asks God to ___ him according to His word.

cards.text: Then he asks God to remove him from the path of deceit and to graciously grant him His law. But he's not just leaving a road. He's already picked a new one.

cards.question: Leaving the path of deceit behind, which way does the writer say he has chosen?
Having chosen his way, the writer says he has set God's ordinances behind him.

cards.text: Now he says he clings to God's testimonies. Remember, he started out clinging to the dust. Now he's holding on to something a WHOLE lot better.

cards.question: Holding on to God's testimonies, the writer asks the LORD not to let him be put to shame.

cards.text: Then he picks up the pace. He says he RUNS in the path of God's commandments. This man went from lying in the dust to running, and me? I go from lying down to lying down a little to the left.

cards.question: Why does the writer say he runs in the path of God's commandments?

answers.text: Because God will enlarge his heart
Because his enemies are close behind
Because the day is nearly done

cards.text: Now he asks again for the LORD to teach him the way of His statutes. And this time he makes a promise about how long he'll keep them.

cards.question: If the LORD teaches him, how long does the writer promise to keep God's statutes?

answers.text: All the way to the end

cards.question: The writer asks God for ___ so he can obey His law and follow it with all his heart.

cards.text: Back at the ovens, baker! Now the writer asks God to direct him in the path of His commandments. And he's got a reason for wanting that path.

cards.question: The writer says the path of God's commandments is where he finds delight.

cards.text: Next he asks God to turn his heart toward His testimonies, and away from one thing in particular. That's a man saying, 'Lord, when the LIMITED TIME OFFER email shows up, hold me back.'

cards.question: What does the writer NOT want his heart turned toward?

cards.text: Then he prays for his eyes: "Turn my eyes away from worthless things; revive me with Your word." Friend, if my eyes got turned away from every worthless thing, I'd lose four hours a day of watching dogs ride skateboards.

cards.question: The writer asks God to establish His word to His servant, to produce ___ for God.

cards.text: Then he asks God to turn away the disgrace he dreads. And he gives a reason for asking.

cards.question: What reason does the writer give when he asks God to turn away the disgrace he dreads?

answers.text: He has never sinned at all

cards.text: "How I long for Your precepts!" And for the third time in this passage, he asks to be revived. Baker, I've asked my oven to preheat faster more times than that, and it STILL doesn't care.

cards.question: Longing for God's precepts, what does the writer ask God to revive him in?

cards.text: Next he asks for God's loving devotion to come to him, and God's salvation, according to His promise.

cards.question: With God's loving devotion and salvation, what does the writer say he'll be able to do?

answers.text: Answer the one who taunts him
Rest from all of his labor
Rebuild the walls of his city

cards.question: The writer says he can answer the one who taunts him because he trusts in his own strength.

cards.text: Then he asks God never to take His word of truth from his mouth, because he hopes in God's judgments. And he promises he'll always obey God's law, forever and ever.

cards.question: Obeying God's law and seeking His precepts, how does the writer say he will walk?

cards.text: Then he gets BOLD. He says he'll speak of God's testimonies before KINGS. Kings, baker! I get nervous leaving a voicemail.

cards.question: The writer says he will be ashamed when he speaks of God's testimonies before kings.
The writer says he delights in God's commandments because he ___ them.

cards.text: He wraps it up by lifting his hands to God's commandments, the ones he loves, and meditating on His statutes. And that's where we'll pull this batch out of the oven, friend. Trust me, this song still has plenty to say.
